claims.text: A hybrid CALPHAD and DFT-trained MTP workflow can accurately predict melting temperature and entropy of fusion in alloys with at least five components.
NbMoTaW is presented as an example of a five- to six-principal-element alloy.
CALPHAD can provide rapid phase-stability filtering and initial solidus estimates using assessed binary interactions.
MTP-based thermodynamic integration trained on DFT data can calculate high-temperature free energies, entropy of fusion, and heat capacity.
The CALPHAD baseline should require a fraction of fully assessed binary systems fAB equal to 1.
At least 370 MPEA compositions are required in the MTP training database to ensure descriptor coverage.
Local lattice distortion and short-range order modify the local vibrational density of states and hence the vibrational contribution to Gibbs free energy.
Mean-field CALPHAD fails to resolve local lattice distortion and short-range order, whereas atomistic MTP simulations resolve them.
The number of distinct binary pairs in an N-component alloy scales as N(N-1)/2.
Increasing the number of binary interactions raises the probability of negative formation enthalpies and therefore promotes intermetallic stabilization.
Configurational entropy in an equimolar N-component alloy scales logarithmically with N.
MTP thermodynamic integration captures nonlinear vibrational-entropy effects from lattice distortion and short-range order that can stabilize solid solutions or shift melting points.
The hybrid method will predict melting temperature and entropy of fusion with an error below 1 meV per atom relative to experiment.
The hybrid method will identify five-component refractory solid solutions stable above 2000 °C that CALPHAD alone incorrectly predicts to form intermetallics or undergo liquid phase separation.
CALPHAD screening found that the solid-solution fraction at the solidus decreases from 30% for three-component alloys to 5% for six-component alloys.
Maximum use temperature decreases as the number of principal elements increases.
The proposed method is limited to equimolar or near-equimolar alloys and should not be applied without significant extrapolation when fAB is below 1.
MTP potentials trained on limited DFT data may not transfer reliably above 3000 °C because anharmonic effects become dominant.
The fAB=1 credibility filter may exclude viable non-equimolar high-temperature compositions.
The hypothesis is falsified if melting-temperature error exceeds 50 °C or if an alloy predicted to be single phase exhibits more than 10 vol.% intermetallics or liquid-phase separation.

contradictions.description: The stated scope requires N≥5 or five to six principal elements, but NbMoTaW, offered as an example, contains only four named elements.

The predicted accuracy is expressed as <1 meV/atom for melting temperature and entropy of fusion, while falsification uses a >50 °C melting-temperature error. The former is not a dimensionally valid temperature-error criterion, and no conversion or consistent tolerance connects the two.
